humanNeedsReview.tier2Rationale: The tier thresholds match exactly -- both sides use revenue >= 10000 -> Platinum, >= 5000 -> Gold, >= 1000 -> Silver, else Bronze on Row.TotalRevenue/row.TotalRevenue -- so the core business rule is faithfully ported. But the timestamp differs in kind: the original VB/C# script sets Row.ProcessedDateTime = DateTime.Now (local server time, evaluated per row at the moment that specific row is processed), while the generated fill returns ProcessedDateTime: ctx.LoadedAtUtc (UTC, and named "LoadedAt" rather than "processed" -- almost certainly a single value captured once for the whole batch/load rather than re-evaluated per row). This is a citable difference in both timezone (local vs UTC) and granularity (per-row wall-clock vs one shared load timestamp), which would change the actual values written to ProcessedDateTime for every row, not just an implementation detail.

Same citable timezone/granularity difference, carried into every row's LoadDateTime.
